content: 1. From the week 24 primary endpoint analysis, Gilead Sciences in Foster City, California, published findings in 2019. 2. Sax PE, Zolopa A, Brar I, Elion R, Ortiz R, Post F, and colleagues conducted a randomized Phase 2 study comparing tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in single-tablet regimens for initial HIV-1 therapy. The results were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2014, volume 67, pages 52–58. 3. Kauppinen KJ, Aho I, and Sutinen J reported that switching from tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) improves lipid profiles and protects against weight gain. This study was published in AIDS in 2022, volume 36, pages 1337–1344. 4. Milinkovic A, Berger F, Arenas-Pinto A, and Mauss S demonstrated that switching from TDF to TAF and back has reversible effects on lipid levels. This study was published in AIDS in 2019, volume 33, pages 2387–2391. 5. Chen R, Zou J, Long L, Huang H, Zhang M, Fan X, and colleagues evaluated the safety and efficacy of tenofovir alafenamide fumarate in early-to-middle pregnancy for mothers with chronic hepatitis B. The findings were published in Frontiers in Medicine (Lausanne) in 2021, volume 8, article 796901. 6. Lockman S, Brummel SS, Ziemba L, Stranix-Chibanda L, McCarthy K, Coletti A, and colleagues conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized, controlled Phase 3 trial (IMPACT 2010/VESTED) to assess the efficacy and safety of dolutegravir with emtricitabine and either TAF or TDF, compared to efavirenz-based regimens, in HIV antiretroviral therapy initiated during pregnancy. The results were published in The Lancet in 2021, volume 397, pages 1276–1292. 7. Schwarz KB, Bezerra J, Choe B, Lin C-H, Abramov F, Nguyen A-H, and colleagues presented a randomized, double-blind evaluation of the pharmacokinetics, safety, and antiviral efficacy of tenofovir alafenamide in children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis B at the EASL International Liver Congress in June 2022, London, UK. 8. Schwarz KB, Bezerra J, Choe B, Lin C-H, Yu J, Abramov F, and colleagues reported on the safety and efficacy of tenofovir alafenamide in children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis B after one year of treatment. 9. The World Health Organization (WHO) published consolidated guidelines in 2021 on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery, and monitoring, emphasizing a public health approach. 10. The WHO Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization met in April 2017 to provide conclusions and recommendations, which were published in the Weekly Epidemiological Record in 2017, volume 92, pages 301–320. 11. The WHO released guidelines on the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B virus, focusing on antiviral prophylaxis during pregnancy. 12. Hyams KC reviewed the risks of chronicity following acute hepatitis B virus infection, with findings published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1995, volume 20, pages 992–1000. 13. The WHO outlined global health sector strategies for HIV, viral hepatitis, and sexually transmitted infections for the period 2022–2030. 14. De Villiers MJ, Nayagam S, and Hallett TB analyzed the impact of timely birth-dose vaccination on the global elimination of hepatitis B, with results published in Nature Communications in 2021, volume 12, article 6223. 15. The WHO published a position paper in July 2017 on hepatitis B vaccines, providing updated recommendations. 16. Interim guidance for country validation of viral hepatitis elimination was released by the WHO. 17. Shimakawa Y, Veillon P, Birguel J, Pivert A, Sauvage V, Guillou-Guillemette HL, and colleagues conducted a longitudinal observational study in Cameroon to assess the residual risk of mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B virus despite timely birth-dose vaccination. The findings were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2022, volume 10, pages e521–e529. 18. Funk AL, Lu Y, Yoshida K, Zhao T, Boucheron P, van Holten J, and colleagues performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy and safety of antiviral prophylaxis during pregnancy to prevent mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B virus. The results were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2021, volume 21, pages 70–84. 19. Thompson P, Morgan CE, Ngimbi P, Mwandagalirwa K, Ravelomanana NLR, Tabala M, and colleagues conducted a feasibility study on preventing vertical transmission of hepatitis B virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The findings were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2021, volume 9, pages e1600–e1609. 20. Nachega JB, Uthman OA, Mofenson LM, Anderson JR, Kanters S, Renaud F, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the safety of TDF-based antiretroviral therapy regimens during pregnancy for HIV-infected women and their infants. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2017, volume 76, pages 1–12.
